feature: Copy a transition from one cut and paste it onto others
summary: Tune a transition at one cut, copy it, and paste it onto another cut, or onto every cut among several picked clips or inside a range: each gets the same kind, length, curve, direction and blur in one undo step. The Transition header's three dots also put a transition back to its usual length.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a recording, cut it twice (or open one with two cuts).

try.do: Put a Cross dissolve on the first cut (stand on it, Command T), then set Length to 0.2s and Curve to Ease in in the panel.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: With that cut still picked, press Command C. The canvas says Copied, Cross dissolve, 0.2s.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Right click the second cut and choose Paste Transition (Copy Transition is greyed there, since that cut is hard).
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Command Z, then Command V with the second cut still picked: the same dissolve lands again.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick two or more clips (or draw a range on the ruler) and press Command V: every cut among them takes it, and the canvas counts how many.
Click the three dots on the Transition header and choose Reset to Default Length: the dissolve goes back to 0.4s and keeps its curve.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does Command C with a cut picked copying the transition, rather than the clip, match what your hands expect from Premiere?
Is it right that Command V with no cut picked lands on the cut the playhead is standing on, the way Command T does?
When a pasted transition is longer than a cut can pay for, it comes in shorter without a word. Do you want the canvas to say so?
Are Copy Transition and Paste Transition easy to find in the cut's right click, between Add Transition and Roll Edit?
rough: The mock's panel menu sits on a Properties header above the cut's sections; the app shows no Properties header while a cut is picked, so for now the three dots sit on the Transition header. Moving them onto the mock's header is task with-a-cut-picked-the-panel-opens-under-the-prop.
Menu rows read Copy Transition and Reset to Default Length in the Mac's Title Case rather than the mock's sentence case (UX-PATTERNS §7).

The app goes further than the mock: Paste Transition sits beside Copy in the panel menu and both are in the cut's right click, and Command X with a cut picked cuts the transition (copies it and takes it off), as Premiere does.
A dip's hold on black is not copied: pasting never puts time into the edit. The cut it lands on keeps the hold it had.
Down arrow moves the playhead to the next cut but leaves the earlier cut picked, so Command V after it pastes on the picked cut, not the one under the playhead. Click or right click the cut you mean.

A cut that cannot pay for the kind at all is refused with the picker's own words and an offer of a dip; a walk could not build such a cut from the sample recording, so that refusal is pinned by a unit test rather than walked.
